questions.q: What must every top-level Apex class declaration include?
options: An access modifier, such as public or global
A constructor, even a default one you write yourself
The virtual keyword
At least one interface in an implements clause
questions.explain: You must use one of the access modifiers (such as public or global) in the declaration of a top-level class; inner classes are the exception.

questions.q: What happens if a class has no user-defined constructor?
options: The class cannot be instantiated at all
Apex throws a compile error demanding a constructor
A default, no-argument public constructor is used
Every method becomes static automatically
questions.explain: You do not need to write a constructor for every class -- if a class does not have a user-defined constructor, a default, no-argument, public constructor is used.

questions.q: Once you write a constructor that takes arguments, what happens to the default no-argument constructor?
options: It still works alongside your new constructor automatically
It's converted into a static method
Apex merges it with your constructor's parameter list
You lose access to it and must write your own no-argument constructor if you still need one
questions.explain: Once you create a constructor for a class, you no longer have access to the default, no-argument public constructor, so you must write your own if you still want one.

questions.q: What syntax lets one constructor call another constructor in the same class (constructor chaining)?
options: super(...)
this(...)
chain(...)
questions.explain: A constructor can call another constructor using the this(...) syntax, also known as constructor chaining.

questions.q: Which statement about Apex constructors is true?
options: A constructor never has an explicit return type and is not inherited
A constructor can declare any return type, including void
A class can only ever have one constructor
Constructors must always be declared private
questions.explain: The syntax for a constructor is similar to a method, but it differs in that a constructor never has an explicit return type, and it is not inherited by objects created from it.
